title: Affine-over-base inclusion preserves directed inverse limits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $J$ a nonempty directed preorder. Let $F:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Aff}/S$ be a diagram in the full subcategory of schemes over $S$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose structure morphisms are affine [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. If $c$ is a limiting cone in this full subcategory, then its image under the inclusion $\mathrm{Aff}/S\to\mathrm{Sch}/S$ is a limiting cone in all schemes over $S$.

source.place: Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), local universal-property argument in its proof, with Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit)

proof.text: Use the relative-spectrum anti-equivalence to send the limiting cone to a colimit of quasi-coherent algebras. Apply the algebra-colimit theorem in all algebra sheaves; its vertex is quasi-coherent, so full-subcategory reflection gives a colimit in quasi-coherent algebras. Uniqueness of colimits identifies it with the image of the given cone, compatibly with every leg. Sections over an affine open U of S are consequently the colimit of the stage section rings.

The relative-spectrum charts and their morphism compatibility identify the restricted cone over every affine U with the spectrum of that ring colimit. The spectrum-colimit theorem gives its universal property for arbitrary test schemes, including tests not affine over U.

For any cone in schemes over S with vertex T, restrict along its S-map to inverse images of affine base opens U. The local spectrum limits give unique factorizations. Choose any index j: the factorization followed by its j-th projection and structure map to U equals the given test-scheme map to U. Hence it is over U and restricts to inverse images of smaller base opens; nonemptiness supplies j. For two affine base opens U and V, cover their intersection by affine opens W; both factorizations restrict over W to the unique factorization. Thus they agree on the overlap, without assuming the intersection itself affine. Glue the local maps to a morphism T to the given vertex. The map is over S and has the required projection composites, since both identities hold on the cover. A second factorization agrees on every open by local uniqueness, hence globally by the gluing uniqueness theorem.
